title: Mitchell's chemiosmotic coupling
body: Peter Mitchell's 1961 paper is titled "Coupling of Phosphorylation to Electron and Hydrogen Transfer by a Chemi-Osmotic type of Mechanism." The claim in the title is specific. The link between electron transport and the making of ATP is chemiosmotic: electron and hydrogen transfer are arranged across a membrane so that they build an electrochemical gradient, and that gradient is what drives phosphorylation. The paper proposes this membrane mechanism in place of treating a high-energy chemical intermediate as the necessary link. It is a theoretical paper in Nature, not a crystal structure of the enzyme. The enzyme that makes the ATP, and the pump that builds related ion gradients, are the subject of the 1997 Nobel Prize, covered in a separate card.
